judge.prompt:
system: You are an evaluation judge. Decide whether one code review finding identifies one specific planted defect. Judge only the defect named, not the location. Return only the requested JSON.
instructions: Input is JSON with "expected", the planted defects at the finding's location (id, file, start, end, defect), and "finding", one reviewer finding (file, start, end, priority, explanation, action).
Return only this JSON object: {"expected":"<id from expected>","verdict":"detects|different-defect","rationale":"<one sentence>"}.
Use "detects" only when the finding describes the same root cause as that planted defect. A finding that shares identifiers, lines or wording but describes another root cause is "different-defect"; then name the closest expected id.
The rationale is one sentence that quotes at least 12 consecutive characters of the finding's explanation or action verbatim inside double quotes.
judge.note: 12 eligible findings, 0 without a valid judge answer; judge cost $0.0228 at Pi catalog prices

records.rationale: The finding identifies the same off-by-one root cause: "The inclusive loop bound allows i to reach len(values)", causing an out-of-bounds panic.
The finding identifies the same nil dereference before error handling, stating "Accessing u.Name before checking err therefore panics".
The finding states "Save returns nil when writing the temporary file fails", identifying the same swallowed write error and false success as the planted defect.
The finding describes a concurrency race where "Concurrent saves to the same path share one temporary file", not a write failure being swallowed by returning nil.
The finding states "Multiple document goroutines read and write total concurrently without synchronization", matching the planted data race and lost-update defect.
The finding states "The search-form email is concatenated directly into SQL." and describes predicate manipulation, identifying the same SQL injection root cause.
The finding identifies the same empty-scores division-by-zero root cause, stating that "encountering such a team causes an integer divide-by-zero panic".
The finding identifies the same command-injection root cause, stating "The web-client-supplied branch is interpolated into a command executed with shell=True."
The finding identifies the same missing end clamp, stating "without bounding it to len(items)", which causes a partial last page to panic.
The finding states "Get returns without unlocking c.mu", identifying the same missing unlock on a cache miss that deadlocks subsequent operations.
The finding states that the comments "merely narrate the initialization, doubling loop, and return statement", which identifies the planted defect that the base-delay comment restates its assignment.
The finding identifies the same unsupported promotional prose defect, stating that "The new rationale uses inflated promotional language" rather than explaining concrete behavior.
